Free low mood tools

20 short exercises on low mood, 2 to 8 minutes each, free and with no account needed. Open one and it runs right in the page.

The 20 tools

  • A week of mood and energy

    Log your mood, your energy, and your sleep each day for a week. They usually move together, and where they do not is interesting.

    7-day log · 2 min

  • What fills you and what drains you

    Sort ordinary activities into ones that leave you with more than you started with and ones that leave you with less.

    Sorter · 5 min

  • Small pleasures still within reach

    Choose ten small pleasures that are genuinely available to you this week. Low mood shrinks the list we can remember; this expands it back.

    Card pick · 4 min

  • How low mood shows up for you

    Rate how often a set of low-mood experiences has been true lately: heaviness, withdrawal, flatness, harsh self-talk.

    Reflection · 5 min

  • Energy cost versus payoff

    Place the tasks and activities in front of you on a grid of how much energy they take against how much they give back.

    Grid · 6 min

  • The tiny first step

    Build a plan for a hard day that is small enough to actually happen: one thing for the body, one for the room, one for connection.

    Plan builder · 5 min

  • Self-talk for hard days

    Turn over cards that show a common harsh thought on one side and a fairer way of saying the same thing on the other. Keep the ones that ring true.

    Perspective cards · 5 min

  • What changed, and when

    Trace back to when your mood started to shift and look at what was different before and after. Sometimes there is a reason hiding in plain sight.

    Guided writing · 7 min

  • When the low patch is heaviest

    Mark the times of day and days of the week when your mood tends to sit lowest. Most people find a shape they had felt but never seen.

    Week map · 3 min

  • The shape of this low patch

    Set a dial for each part of how low mood is sitting with you right now: heaviness, interest, appetite for people, pace, hope. Two low patches can have very different shapes.

    Dials · 4 min

  • How much smaller life has gotten

    Tick the ways your world has quietly shrunk lately. Low mood tends to narrow life in small, reasonable-looking steps, so most of these go unnoticed until they are listed.

    Noticing list · 3 min

  • The waking breath

    Three seconds in through the nose, three seconds out through the mouth, sitting up. A brisker, even rhythm for the mornings when the body does not want to start.

    Breathing · 2 min

  • Five minutes, before and after

    Rate your mood, do one small thing for five minutes, rate it again. A tiny experiment in whether action can move mood, run with your own numbers rather than anyone else's claims.

    Guided exercise · 8 min

  • What to protect when the tank is low

    Put the basics in order of what you would protect first when energy is scarce. On a low day, not everything can be kept up, and deciding in advance is easier than deciding while in it.

    Ranking · 4 min

  • Where a low day's hours go

    Divide 100 points across how the waking hours of a typical low day actually go: in bed awake, scrolling, obligations, screens, outside, with people. Seeing it in bars is different from knowing it vaguely.

    Budget · 4 min

  • What is under the low

    Narrow the feeling inside a low patch from a rough word to a precise one, find where it sits in your body, and hear what it might be asking for. "Low" covers a lot of different things.

    Feelings wheel · 3 min

  • A fact, or the mood talking?

    Sort the kinds of things a low day says into facts, mood-talk, and not sure. They arrive in the same voice, which is why the mood's version is so convincing.

    Sorter · 5 min

  • A note for the next low day

    Write a short note today, from a slightly better place, to be read on the next hard day: what helped, what not to believe, who to call. Future you will not remember any of it without this.

    Guided writing · 8 min

  • Mood, daylight, and people: a week

    Log your mood, how much daylight you got, and how much real contact you had, each day for a week. Two of these are things you can change; the third tends to follow them.

    7-day log · 2 min

  • Who helps on a low day

    Place the people in your life on a grid of how much effort it takes to see them against how you feel afterward. On a low day, effort and afterglow do not always line up.

    Grid · 6 min

What these tools are, and are not

Every tool here is free and works without an account: choose cards, move dials, sort a list, follow a paced breath, or keep a seven-day log, and read back what you noticed at the end. They are built to make a vague feeling more specific, which is often the first useful step.

None of them diagnoses, screens for or treats anything, and nothing you see at the end is a score or a label. If something you notice worries you, a licensed therapist is the right next conversation, and the directory is free to browse.
